column2: We will establish military production in Abilia: four military factories and four building slots. The workshops will not deliver a ready assault formation before the uprising, but they will be able to replace losses after the first battles. The military committee will not receive funding for a separate reinforced formation.

When the split occurs, Abilia and its four military factories pass to the resistance. Until the division, their output enters the common state stockpile; production is assigned through the normal interface.

Republic of the Districts
The republic's civilian institutions, restored economy and professional army. Post-war decisions determine their combined capabilities.
The Renewed Presidium
Permanent Party administration, industrial planning and a regular army. Their capabilities depend on the chosen model of post-war reconstruction.
Our side has won the civil war and its wartime programmes have ended.

If no suitable site is available, the treasury will receive a construction reserve instead of a new factory: £ADISCORD_economy_treasury_texticon §Y900§!. The permanent industrial specialisation is retained.
Services Return to the Districts
Residents need doctors, postmen and civil servants as much as they need a new constitution. We will open a paid public-services programme and restore trust in the new administration.
District Administrations
Military commandants will transfer economic affairs to permanent administrations. Common rules will reduce expenditure and spare the cabinet from settling every local dispute.
Restore the Registers

Without records of residents, property and obligations, neither benefits nor taxes can be administered. Archivists and local councils will bring the surviving documents together. Nodrul will be notified that its former mandate is under review.
Retain Local Personnel
We will retain specialists who took no part in repression. Swift reconciliation will build trust, but command will have to accommodate the diversity of the new administration.
Review Appointments
District commissions will review appointments. The cabinet will gain a more dependable administration at the cost of prolonged disputes and weaker local support.
Civil Service Charter
We will define officials' responsibilities, the complaints procedure and the limits of district administrations' powers. These rules will apply under any future political settlement.
Reconnect the Economy
We will link the capital to district centres and restore road services. The first works will improve one road, while further construction will proceed faster.
Bring Working Families Home
Housing and reliable roads will allow evacuated families to return. We can then finance the reopening of workshops where returning specialists will work.
Cooperative Workshops
We will bring small workshops together in durable production cooperatives. A new civilian factory will serve as the model for the next wave of construction.
Arsenals under Civilian Oversight

The army will retain the arms-production capacity it needs, but its operations will be brought into the public state budget. We will restore one factory and organise supplies to the plants already operating.
An Economy without Emergency Orders
We will coordinate orders for civilian workshops and arsenals so that they no longer compete for the same workers and machinery. Production will receive a steady flow of work.
Register the Frontline Units
We will bring separate detachments into a common army register and open a personnel-training programme. The divisions will remain, but replacements and supplies will be centrally organised.
School for Field Commanders
Resistance commanders will teach new officers the lessons that helped their units survive. A common curriculum will combine junior commanders' initiative with regular training.
District Supply Service
District depots will operate to a common schedule. Units will recover their combat readiness faster and lose fewer supplies in transit.
The Republic's Professional Army
Standing formations will receive common service regulations and replacement training. This is the foundation both for defending the passes and for future campaigns abroad.
Conclude Emergency Reconstruction

Civilian services, workshops and the regular army must be functioning before the emergency budget closes. Completing three paid programmes will consolidate industrial growth and restore the population's confidence.
The State after Ivanov

Victory preserved the Party, but did not restore the old system of government. Hedersett must rebuild the ministries, industry and the guard, then define relations between the centre and the district organisations. An agreement with local elites and an emergency chain of command are distinct domestic courses. Relations with Nodrul are settled separately.
District Secretariats
We will restore a single chain of administration from the presidium to the districts. Permanent secretariats will reduce the expense of parallel commissions and speed up the execution of decisions.
Wartime Lists
Party files list rebels and draft evaders alongside engineers who failed to obtain permission to evacuate. A review of their cases will determine whom we return to work and whom we declare an enemy.
An Agreement with District Elites

We will bring specialists back and recognise the district organisations' role in reconstruction. The course that follows will formalise their powers and retain local personnel. This will accelerate civilian work at the cost of some freedom for the central secretariat.
An Emergency Party Hierarchy

Hedersett regards uncertainty over appointments as the continuation of war by other means. We will establish personnel commissions and a single chain of command. A security reserve will become a separate paid measure. Strengthening the centre comes at the price of purges, the costs of oversight and the loss of specialists.
Charter of the Party State

After the congress of district secretariats or the creation of an executive secretariat, we will establish a permanent framework for the Party state. The charter does not erase the chosen model: the negotiated system preserves local initiative, while the hierarchy preserves central control. Military, economic and foreign-policy choices remain independent.
Restore the Routes to the Ports
Military transport disrupted the districts' links to the coast. We will restore a common plan for the road services so that cargo can reach the ports again and workers can reach their factories.
Labour District Reception Offices

District reception offices will match workforce registers with housing and returning families. We can then finance the reconstruction of one controlled port district: a civilian factory and its access routes.
Restore the Resort Economy

Before the war, coastal revenue sustained a substantial part of the state apparatus. We will restore civilian enterprises and allow the houses to resume servicing ports and resorts. These funds can no longer be promised to defence plants at the same time.
War Orders instead of the Season
We will postpone the return of the holiday season: materials, workers and new capacity will go to defence enterprises. The army will grow stronger sooner, but the civilian economy will have to wait.
The Post-war Production Plan

Commercial reconstruction or the defence combine has already determined the economy's priority. We will now bring taxation, capital expenditure and production plans together in a normal post-war budget. The differences between the two models remain; this shared focus merely ends emergency administration.
Take Stock of the Internal Forces

The internal troops won the struggle for government, but their departmental rolls are no basis for a regular army. We will count the units and open a paid re-equipment programme: weapons, support equipment and trucks will enter the common army stockpile.
A Headquarters, Not a Commandant's Office
Commanders were trained to guard buildings and suppress unrest. Now they must prepare operations involving several formations, work with maps and maintain communications with neighbouring units.
Supply the Border Units

We will make logistics the organising principle of the new army. Permanent depots and unified accounting will replace departmental allocations, while border units receive priority according to actual need. This course leads to district defence corps and rules out reliance on an independent field headquarters.
An Army beyond the Capital

We will make field service the organising principle of the new army. The internal troops will adopt a common programme of manoeuvres, joint exercises and commander training for multi-formation operations. This course leads to a field general staff and rules out deep specialisation in district logistics.
End Emergency Rule

Emergency rule can end only after four questions have been settled: how Party authority is organised, how the economy earns its revenue, what kind of army the country maintains, and on what terms it exists alongside Nodrul. Unfinished purges will then cease, and the presidium will take responsibility for the state's ordinary life.
Congress of District Secretariats

Compromise must become an institution rather than a series of personal promises. The district secretariats will receive a regular congress and the right to coordinate some economic decisions in advance. The centre loses a little operational freedom, but gains predictable execution, a tax base and fewer reasons to govern through emergency commissions again.
Executive Secretariat

A single chain of orders needs a body that checks compliance every day. The executive secretariat will bring appointments, reporting and departmental oversight into one administration. Decisions will cost the centre less and move faster politically, but constant pressure on the districts will leave its mark on internal stability.
